text:
ash: quick follow-up on the continuous-batching refactor—i sketched some ideas for separating the 'queue surface' from coalescing semantics, want quick opinions :thinking:
joan: sounds useful. what's the concrete problem we're solving vs current admission API?
mike: we keep hitting tail latency when small requests get stuck behind large ones. current queue exposes too many internals to scheduler, makes the admission logic messy.
sara: +1. i think we want a minimal contract: enqueue returns a handle and a 'visibility' hint for coalescer, not raw slot pointers.
lee: can we define the contract as: enqueue(req) -> {ticket, deadline_hint, cost_units} and then coalescer can decide to merge or isolate?
ash: (ops-bot) deploy queued: runtime/continuous-batcher v2 -> canary started
ash: small nit: who owns eviction decisions? runtime or queue?
ash: (sorry, meant ash)
joan: eviction should be a queue-level policy surface but pluggable from runtime. runtime sends QoS class and budget, queue decides best eviction/pack strategy. keep ownership clear.
mike: tradeoff: if queue exposes eviction hooks, runtime can implement tenant-aware policies but coupling increases. if runtime keeps all policies, queue stays simple but needs richer telemetry.
sara: proposal: keep queue surface minimal (ticket, hint, observable counters), allow runtime to register policy adapters for eviction/preemption. adapters are opaque to queue.
lee: adapters are fine but we need perf budget: adapter callbacks must be async and bounded, cannot block enqueue path. otherwise we regress p99.
ash: (ops-bot) canary report: 10% traffic, p50 unchanged, p95 +2ms, investigating
ash: (again, ash) right — callback must be scheduled off-path. queue only raises signals: e.g., "pressure: level=2, candidate_ids=[..]" and runtime consumes stream.
joan: agree. also need a way to annotate requests with 'coalesce affinity' so we don't merge requests that break semantics (e.g., tool-calls).
mike: suggest simple enum on req: {COALESCE_OK, COALESCE_SOFT, COALESCE_NO}. default COALESCE_SOFT.
sara: +1. docs + tests needed for libcall patterns.
lee: about headroom: queue should advertise headroom estimate per lane (tokens free vs reserved) so runtime can do early backpressure. but estimate is best-effort.
ash: (ops-bot) canary update: p95 improved after throttle tweak, rolling out more
ash: (ash) migration plan idea: 1) add minimal ticket contract 2) runtime registers adapter but disabled 3) enable adapter for limited tenants 4) iterate on adapter API
joan: fallback plan? if adapter crashes we must disable it and keep default queue policy. can't let a bad adapter take down node.
mike: include health-check heartbeat for adapters and circuit-breaker.
sara: observability: surface per-ticket lifecycle events to tracing (enqueue, coalesce-merge, evict, dispatch). that'll make debugging easier.
lee: also expose queue-length-by-cost-unit metric. helps correlate with p99.
ash: (ops-bot) canary: 30% traffic, two adapters enabled for internal tenants, no errors reported
ash: (ash) ok next steps — i'll draft a slim RFC with the ticket contract + adapter interface and async signaling. want people to review before friday.
joan: ack, i'll add notes on safety boundaries and fallback behaviors.
mike: i'll prototype a tiny adapter to validate perf overhead.
sara: i'll add test cases for coalesce enum.
lee: i'll draft telemetry and headroom metrics.
ash: (ops-bot) reminder: eng-runtime sync in 1h
ash: thanks all :thumbsup:
